* MariaDB 12.3+ added two new reserved words, `CONVERSION` and `TO_DATE`
* MySQL 8.0.23+'s AUTOEXTEND_SIZE table option can now be used in diff operations (c69ce44)
* MySQL's July 2026 server releases have un-reserved `PARALLEL` (reserved in 8.2.0+) and `MANUAL` (reserved in 8.4.0+) per resolution of [server bug #114874](https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=114874)

* The [user](https://www.skeema.io/docs/options/#user) option now provides a clear error if the configured username contains a colon, which isn't supported due to a limitation in the database driver DSN format (62e8d57)
* Database server version/flavor detection logic has been made more robust, to account for MySQL's switch to YY.M versioning starting with MySQL 26.7 (5cc5cb0)

* [Aurora 8.4 strictly requires TLS](https://www.skeema.io/blog/2024/05/14/mysql84-surprises/#:~:text=Aurora%20MySQL%208.4) for all connections, so Skeema's [SSH tunnel](https://www.skeema.io/docs/features/ssh/) functionality no longer auto-disables TLS when using [flavor=aurora:8.4](https://www.skeema.io/docs/options/#flavor) or when the flavor isn't known yet
* MySQL 5.6-5.7 and MariaDB 10.2-10.3 are now deprecated (but still supported in Skeema v1)
* **MySQL 9.7 support** (b2f241f, 23b85cd)

Four fixes, no new surface.

- External units created by an integration keep a bare host, so they can be edited and set as the gateway again (#1968, reported by @harpyeagle in #1056).
- A Proxmox host and its untagged guests no longer show another client's VLAN (#1757, @MassiPi).
- One unit is one SSH connection again, instead of two (#1893, @crowedavid).
- An unknown uptime shows "—" instead of a real-looking "0d 0h" (#55, @harpyeagle).

Units that will never run the agent are now first class. A router with very little flash, or one where the package simply does not fit, used to be a second-class unit: it showed up in the fleet, but its inventory was a guess, its config backup was only possible by hand and the weekly schedule ignored it entirely. This release gives it an inventory mode of its own, the config backup over SSH from the fleet list, and the same backup on schedule. In parallel, the agent that does fit small devices now ships com

Agent self-upgrade works again. The previous release packed the agent binaries with UPX, and the startup guard that checks the embedded agent version scanned the raw bytes for a version string that compression had hidden. The server therefore started with agent upgrades disabled, so every fix that travels inside the agent was unreachable. The build now writes a small version stamp next to the binaries and the server reads it first, keeping the byte scan as a fallback for unpacked builds. Nothing else change

- **An automatic backup no longer fails with `archive/tar: write too long` on a live server.** The archive sized the database entry from a `stat` and then copied until EOF, so a database that grew between the two calls wrote more bytes than the header declared.
